Question:
Three distinct lines intersect at the same point \(O\). Counting each angle smaller than a straight angle formed by any two noncollinear rays as one angle, how many pairs of vertical angles are there in the figure?

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_063_q5_question_en.svg)
Solution: The total number of angles smaller than a straight angle formed by pairs of the \(6\) rays is \(C(6,2)-3=12\). Each angle has exactly one vertical angle, so there are \(12\div2=6\) pairs.
